Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Acute unilateral throbbing headache with visual aura, photophobia, nausea/vomiting; normal neurologic review → most consistent with migraine with aura.  
- Risk factors (recent estrogen OCP) and positional worsening raise possibility of cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST); likelihood moderate per DDx although not discussed by clinician.  
- Intracranial mass/tumor considered by patient; low likelihood given acute presentation, absence of progressive symptoms or focal deficits.  
- Plan: clinician advised strong analgesia (paracetamol or co-codamol plus NSAID), initiate headache diary, arrange follow-up next week, and provided red-flag safety-netting (worsening headache, neurologic symptoms, visual changes).  

Management Plan
-  Provide analgesics: Paracetamol or Co-codamol (dose/route/frequency not documented) and NSAID (Ibuprofen or Naproxen; dose/route/frequency not documented).  
-  Initiate headache diary to identify triggers and frequency.  
-  Consider prophylactic migraine medication if headaches persist; to be reviewed at next appointment.  
-  Safety-netting advice given: return immediately if headache worsens, persists >2–3 days, or any focal neurologic deficits/vision changes occur.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Migraine with visual aura – High likelihood: matches unilateral throbbing pain, aura, photophobia, nausea/vomiting, positive family history, absence of neuro deficits.  
2. Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis – Moderate likelihood: new severe headache, positional component, recent estrogen OCP use; no focal signs but warrants consideration.  
3. Intracranial mass / brain tumour – Low likelihood: headache with vomiting but no progressive course or neurologic deficits.
